report.headline: High-usage G League scorer projected to a near-average NBA role, with an unreliable shooting forecast

projection.text: Projected usage rate in the NBA is 19.9%, down from 26.1% in the G League, landing almost exactly at the league-average usage of 20.1% for the target season.

risks.text: The estimate rests on only 45 historical GL->NBA transitions, a thin cohort for a move of this kind.
The true-shooting model is no better than simply assuming the league-mean true shooting percentage, so its 56.6% projection should not be relied upon.
Both projections carry wide uncertainty bands: usage spans 14.5%-25.4% at 80% confidence and 11.6%-28.3% at 95%; true shooting spans 49.9%-63.4% at 80% and 46.4%-66.9% at 95%.
Two full seasons passed between the source season and the move, adding time-based uncertainty not captured by the single-season snapshot of production.

strengths.text: Elite statistical production in the source season: 25.4 points, 11.2 rebounds per 75 possessions, a 63.7% true shooting mark, and a 26.1% usage rate.
That production placed the player well above the G League average, at +1.27 standard deviations in usage and +1.42 standard deviations in true shooting.
For usage specifically, the model beats the best trivial baseline (3.3% error vs. 4.3%), so the usage projection carries real information.

The fitted transition slopes indicate roughly 53% of a player's usage advantage and about 80% of their true-shooting advantage over their league tend to carry across this move, consistent with a meaningful but damped translation of the source-season standing.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage runs from 14.5% to 25.4%, a span of roughly two standard deviations of the league's usage spread (5.4%), so the model can rank this player against others but cannot pin down a single value. The true-shooting projection of 56.6% should not be treated as informative at all: its out-of-fold error (4.7%) is no better than the trivial league-mean baseline (4.7%), which the model needs to beat to be trusted.
